_meta.source_notes: MSRPs (excluding destination) reflect the current US model year (MY2026 or MY2027) from manufacturer sites and automotive press as of September 2026. Ranges and efficiency are EPA figures from fueleconomy.gov unless a vehicle's notes say otherwise (some city/highway splits are derived from EPA MPGe). winter_range_mi is our derated WV estimate (~28% haircut). highway_range_mi is a realistic sustained 70-mph range: originally curated per model, and in the September 2026 refresh scaled from the new EPA range using each model's previous ratio (new models use ~80% of EPA, ~68% for Tesla). US/Canadian parts % is from NHTSA's MY2026 AALA report where listed. Spec fields not used by the calculator (home_max_kw, dcfc_peak_kw, cargo, towing) are informational; where a vehicle's notes don't vouch for them, treat them as unverified. Per-field confidence is documented at /state-of-the-data — refresh MSRPs quarterly.
_meta.status_values: current = sold new; final_year = production ended or last model year, new dealer inventory remains; discontinued = no longer sold new (kept for used-market shoppers and old shared links; msrp_usd is the last new price).
_meta.id_note: IDs are stable keys used in shareable calculator URLs. They do not track model year — an id ending in -2025 may describe a 2027 vehicle. Never rename an id.
_meta.curation_criteria: Selected for relevance to WV buyers: mix of price points, SUV/truck emphasis, AWD options, reliable dealer presence in WV or bordering states, PHEV options for range-anxious rural buyers, and several long-range luxury BEVs that also serve the used-market shopper.

vehicles.notes: Dominant US EV SUV. Supercharger access. Verify pricing after recent Tesla adjustments. Formerly 'Long Range AWD' — Tesla renamed it 'Premium' in 2026 and raised the price $1,000 (May 2026). Battery size and 10–80% time are not published by Tesla; values are estimates.
Efficient sedan, strong Supercharger network. Formerly 'Long Range RWD' (renamed 'Premium' in 2026). A cheaper Model 3 Standard is also in the catalog.
Most compelling mid-priced BEV SUV for WV market. Native NACS port from MY2027. Earlier data wrongly listed Ingersoll, Ontario assembly and understated energy use.
Pickup is the top-selling body style in WV. Home-backup power feature is a real selling point.
vehicles.status_note: Ford cancelled the battery-electric Lightning in Dec 2025 (an extended-range successor is planned). Leftover/used only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.notes: Extended Range battery (131 kWh) — 320 mi EPA. ~$15k more than Standard Range but real-world WV highway range jumps to ~245 mi. Better fit for long trips.
vehicles.status_note: Ford cancelled the battery-electric Lightning in Dec 2025 (an extended-range successor is planned). Leftover/used only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.notes: Extended Range — 410 mi EPA (InsideEVs 70-mph test on the 2025 LT Extended Range: 310 mi). Strong for contractors / fleet use in WV. MY2027 (production from Oct 2026) switches to a native NACS port and adds ~$200–400. The cheaper WT Standard Range is now in the catalog as a trim of this card. Towing is the Extended Range rating from GM Fleet and dealer specs (12,500 lb; the April figure of 10,000 lb was too low). Battery size is an estimate.

Premium adventure truck. Limited WV dealer presence. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs — heavy vehicles not required to disclose parts content). Rivian dropped the 'Dual Standard' LFP pack for MY2027; Premium (old Large pack) is now the entry trim. Range on standard 20-inch wheels. Battery and charge time approximate. Peak DC kW for MY2027 not published; the figure shown carries over from 2026.

Largest pack option — ~140 kWh / 380 mi EPA (20-inch wheels). AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs). $7k step up from Premium for meaningful extra range. Old 'Max' pack, renamed Premium Long Range for MY2027. Battery approximate.
Established Ford dealer network in WV makes service convenient.

Premium with Extended Range 91 kWh pack — 320 mi EPA. Meaningful step up from Select Standard Range for WV drivers who regularly do longer trips. MSRP is approximate (Premium $40,595 + Extended Range option ~$5,245); confirm on ford.com.
Class-leading DCFC speed. Assembled in Georgia (Metaplant opened 2024). Hyundai cut Ioniq 5 prices ~$9k for MY2026 after the federal credit ended (+$250 for MY2027).

Long Range 84 kWh pack — 318 mi EPA. Same 800V ultra-fast DCFC. Common step-up trim for WV buyers who want highway range without Tesla pricing. Hyundai cut Ioniq 5 prices ~$9k for MY2026. Hyundai publishes 10–80% in ~20 min but no peak kW; the 235 kW figure is from independent tests of earlier models.
Shares 800V platform with Ioniq 5. Fast DCFC. Highest US/CA parts content of any EV on this list (MY2025 AALA). Kia cut EV6 prices ~$5k for MY2026. US/Canadian parts % is the MY2025 figure.

Wind trim with 84 kWh Long Range pack — 319 mi EPA. Same 800V platform as Ioniq 5 LR. Topped the 2025 AALA index at 80% US/CA parts. Light Long Range RWD ($41,200) is a cheaper way to get the 84 kWh pack. US/Canadian parts % is the MY2025 figure.

All-new 3rd-gen Leaf on Nissan's AmpR Medium platform (shared with Ariya), now a crossover SUV rather than a hatchback. 75 kWh pack, 303 mi EPA, native NACS DCFC at 150 kW. MY2025 was the outgoing 40 kWh / 149 mi / CHAdeMO 2nd-gen carryover; this row reflects the fall-2025 3rd-gen that dealers are actually selling. Japan-built. One of the cheapest new EVs (with the Chevy Bolt). The cheaper 52 kWh 'S' trim was cancelled/delayed; S+ charges at 7.2 kW at home (higher trims may differ).
Larger, more traditional SUV format. 2LT trim no longer offered; LT FWD is the closest equivalent. Native NACS from MY2027.
Assembled in Tennessee. The 62 kWh Standard trim was dropped; Pro RWD is now the entry trim. US/Canadian parts % is the MY2025 figure.
vehicles.status_note: Chattanooga production ended April 2026; MY2026 dealer inventory expected into 2027.

vehicles.notes: Pro S trim with 82 kWh larger battery — 291 mi EPA. TN-assembled. 3 yrs Electrify America included.
vehicles.status_note: Chattanooga production ended April 2026; MY2026 dealer inventory expected into 2027.

vehicles.notes: GM platform under Honda skin. Strong Honda dealer network in WV. Assembled in Mexico despite Honda branding. Honda cut MSRP $7,500 in April 2026 but reduced dealer cash by about the same amount, so real transaction prices barely moved.
vehicles.status_note: Honda ends Prologue sales after MY2026; no Honda EV is planned for the US in 2027.

vehicles.notes: Toyota reliability reputation. Manufactured in Japan. Renamed from bZ4X to bZ for 2026 with a larger battery and NACS port. AWD XLE is $39,900 / 288 mi; base XLE FWD (57.7 kWh) is $34,980 / 236 mi.

Excellent WV option: ~52 mi electric covers most commutes, gas backup eliminates range anxiety. Assembled in Japan. New-generation replacement for the RAV4 Prime. Electric range (52 mi; some sources say 54 for SE) and hybrid-mode mpg (40) are Toyota projections — not yet EPA-listed. Total range uses Toyota's '490+ mi' (other sources claim 550–600). SE charges at 7 kW with no DC fast charging (XSE/Woodland get 11 kW and CCS).
Ford dealer ubiquity in WV. Final model year, single trim ($35,400 + $1,495 destination).
vehicles.status_note: Production ended Dec 2025. Leftover dealer stock only.

vehicles.notes: Off-road capable with electric assist. Popular body style in WV; shorter EV-only range. Previous data listed 49 kWh/100mi — that was the MPGe figure, not kWh. EPA electric-mode use is 68 kWh/100mi.
vehicles.status_note: Stellantis ended all North American plug-in hybrids in Jan 2026. Used market only.

vehicles.notes: Most efficient non-Tesla EV. Aerodynamic sedan shape. Assembled in South Korea — 0% US/CA content.
vehicles.status_note: Hyundai dropped the regular Ioniq 6 from the US for MY2026 (only the ~$70k Ioniq 6 N remains). Used market only.

vehicles.notes: Small premium crossover. US production moved from China to Belgium for MY2026 and the price dropped ~$6k; the 'Core' trim is gone.
vehicles.status_note: Volvo is ending US EX30 sales in 2026 (dealer order cutoff March 2026); remaining inventory only.

vehicles.notes: Practical, reliable. Slower DCFC than Kia EV6. Assembled in South Korea.
vehicles.status_note: MY2026 is the Niro EV's final model year; dealer inventory only.

vehicles.notes: Flagship 3-row family EV. US-assembled since late 2024. Biggest recent addition to the family-SUV EV segment. Previously listed as 'Wind RWD', which doesn't exist; the specs match Light Long Range RWD. Kia has been running ~$10k customer cash on the EV9.
Premium US-assembled EV on GM platform. GM dealer network broad in WV.
Benchmark PHEV efficiency — ~51 mpg on gas, 44 mi all-electric. Japan-assembled. Renamed from Prius Prime. Efficiency figures are MY2025 EPA; MY2027 EPA listing pending.
Badge-engineered twin of the Toyota bZ (formerly bZ4X) with Subaru AWD. Strong Subaru dealer presence in WV. Japan-assembled. Larger 74.7 kWh battery and NACS port from MY2026. Standard AWD.
Entry-luxury BMW EV sedan. Germany-built. Earlier data used the discontinued eDrive35's $52,200 price; eDrive40 is $57,900.
Volvo/Geely sub-brand. China-assembled — no IRA credit and subject to import tariffs.
vehicles.status_note: Withdrawn from the US (tariffs and the connected-vehicle rule bar MY2027+). Used market only.

vehicles.notes: Polarizing design but high mindshare. Highway range derated further than Model Y/3 due to massive frontal area. A cheaper Dual Motor AWD trim ($69,990, same EPA range) launched in 2026. 10–80% time is a third-party estimate.
Popular luxury PHEV. 40 mi electric covers most commutes. SC-assembled. MY2026 EPA figures; MSRP approximate. A new-generation 2027 X5 50e xDrive ($77,500, ~44 mi electric est.) arrives October 2026.

3-row SUV sibling of R1T. AALA-exempt (GVWR >8,500 lbs). Rivian dropped the 'Dual Standard' LFP pack for MY2027; Premium is now the entry trim. Battery and charge time approximate. Peak DC kW for MY2027 not published; the figure shown carries over from 2026.
Large pack variant — 135 kWh / 352 mi EPA. AALA-exempt. $5k step up for meaningful extra range on long trips.
Entry-luxury Mercedes EV SUV. Compact platform, 5-seat. Hungary-assembled — no IRA credit. Slowest DCFC of the Mercedes lineup (100 kW peak).
vehicles.status_note: Discontinued in the US after MY2025. Used market only. The new electric CLA is Mercedes' entry EV.

vehicles.notes: Mid-tier Mercedes executive EV sedan. Germany-assembled — no IRA credit.
vehicles.status_note: MY2026 is the final model year for the EQE sedan.

vehicles.notes: US-assembled at Mercedes' Tuscaloosa plant. Popular mid-size luxury SUV. EPA-listed for MY2027, though some reports say EQE production ends in 2026 — confirm availability with a dealer.

charging.connector_dcfc: CCS (Tesla Supercharger access via NACS adapter)

vehicles.notes: EPA range champion of the US market at 512 mi (19-inch wheels). 21-inch wheels drop to 446 mi. Class-leading 19.2 kW onboard charger. Tesla Supercharger access opened in 2024 via Lucid-provided NACS adapter. Used-market relevance: early Air GT depreciation has been steep.

Lucid's first SUV; 3-row seating with optional 6-seat captain's chairs. 400 kW peak DCFC is class-leading — adds ~200 mi in 11 min on a 350 kW+ charger. Native NACS DCFC port, so Superchargers are plug-and-charge. Rare in WV dealer inventory; most sales online-direct.

Mercedes flagship luxury sedan — 390 mi EPA (MY2026), one of the longest-range German EVs sold in the US. German-assembled. Used-market shoppers: early EQS (2022-2023) depreciated heavily, strong used-buyer value. Refreshed for 2027 (800-volt, 122 kWh). Range and efficiency shown are MY2026 EPA values; MY2027 ratings pending.

Tesla flagship sedan, 410 mi EPA. MY2026 price cut to $74,990 before Tesla ceased Model S/X production in April 2026 — dealer and used-market inventory remains active. Highway range in practice typically 290–320 mi (Tesla EPA is known to overstate; WV elevation and cold compound this). Supercharger network access is the main practical advantage.
vehicles.status_note: Production ended May 2026. Used market only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.notes: Model Y Performance — 3.3s 0-60, uprated brakes, lowered suspension, 21-inch wheels. Range drops ~25 mi vs LR due to wheels/motor. Updated for the 2026 new-body Model Y Performance ($57,990 after a $500 increase in May 2026; 306 mi EPA). Battery size and charge time are unconfirmed estimates.

Model 3 Performance — 2.9s 0-60, track-tuned suspension, adaptive dampers. Fastest sub-$60k EV sedan on the market. MY2027 EPA figures (316 mi); price unchanged at $54,990. Battery size is unconfirmed.

Dual-motor Performance (now the Premium trim's $5,000 power upgrade) — 665 hp, 3.4s 0-60, same tow/payload as Standard. For MY2027 the standard pack is ~108.5 kWh usable (300 mi EPA on 20-inch wheels); the Long Range pack (~140 kWh, 380 mi) is an upgrade. Rivian renamed trims for MY2027: its new 'Performance' trim is the former tri-motor (~$101k), not this dual-motor version. Price = Premium + $5,000 power upgrade; destination extra.

Dual-motor Performance (now the Premium trim's $5,000 power upgrade) — 665 hp, 3.4s 0-60 for a 3-row full-size SUV. For MY2027 the standard pack is ~108.5 kWh usable (300 mi EPA on 20-inch wheels); the Long Range pack (~140 kWh, 380 mi) is an upgrade. Rivian renamed trims for MY2027: its new 'Performance' trim is the former tri-motor (~$101k), not this dual-motor version. Price = Premium + $5,000 power upgrade; destination extra.

Cadillac flagship EV — 200 kWh battery (largest in class), ~460 mi range (Cadillac estimate), 750 hp in Velocity Max launch mode. Same Detroit plant as Silverado EV. Not EPA-labeled (too heavy), so range and efficiency are manufacturer/third-party figures. MSRP approximate ($130,300 including destination). MY2027 adds a native NACS port.
Nissan mid-size EV crossover, 87 kWh long-range pack. Slow home-charging (7.2 kW) — plan for overnight. Japan-built. Trim corrected (there is no 'SV' Ariya; the 87 kWh FWD trim is Evolve+).
vehicles.status_note: Nissan dropped the Ariya from the US for MY2026. Used/leftover only; price shown is the last new MSRP.

vehicles.notes: Silverado EV twin with Denali trim — premium interior, same ~170 kWh Extended Range pack, 410 mi EPA. Corrected: the 205 kWh pack is the Max Range version (~478 mi, ~$101k). Highway range matches the mechanically identical Silverado EV Extended Range. MSRP approximate ($80,495 including destination). MY2027 adds NACS.

Acura's first EV, built on GM Ultium at Spring Hill alongside Cadillac Lyriq and Honda Prologue. Only MY2024 was sold (the id says 2025 but is kept so shared links work). 10–80% figure is Acura's 20–80% time.
vehicles.status_note: Acura ended ZDX production in September 2025. Used market only; price shown is the 2024 launch MSRP.

vehicles.notes: Stellantis electric muscle car — retuned Fratzonic exhaust audio, 496 hp R/T dual motor AWD. Canada-assembled. EPA range is for 18-inch wheels (308 mi on 20-inch). Battery is usable capacity.
vehicles.status_note: Dodge dropped the R/T after MY2025; only leftover R/Ts remain. MY2027 is Scat Pack only ($72,495).

vehicles.notes: Returns for 2027 with an LFP battery and native NACS. Cheapest new EV in the catalog ($28,995 with destination). City/highway split derived from EPA MPGe.

Priced August 2026. Light FWD ($29,890, 221 mi) and Wind AWD ($38,690, 280 mi) also offered. US-market EV3s are built in Mexico (production started Aug 2026; the earliest units may be Korean-built). Peak DC ~128 kW is the European spec; Kia US publishes only 10–80% times.

Cheaper, de-contented Model Y (late 2025). Standard AWD is $41,990 / 294 mi. Battery (~69.5 kWh usable) and 7.7 kW home charging are from press reviews; Tesla doesn't publish them. 10–80% time is an estimate.

Cheaper Model 3 trim (late 2025). Tesla doesn't publish battery size or charge times: battery is assumed to match the Model Y Standard (same 321-mi EPA range and efficiency), and home charging (~7.7 kW) and 10–80% time are unconfirmed estimates.

With the F-150 Lightning cancelled, this is the cheapest full-size electric pickup. EPA figures are MY2026 (2027 carries over). Towing (8,500 lb) and payload (2,350 lb) are GM Fleet's MY2026 WT Standard Range figures; 2027 ratings not yet published. Battery size is a third-party estimate; whether MSRP includes destination is unconfirmed; 10–80% time not published.
Standard AWD. Shares the 74.7 kWh battery with the bZ, Solterra, Trailseeker, and Uncharted. Not rated to tow.
Wagon-style electric Subaru with standard AWD and a 3,500 lb tow rating — a natural fit for WV. 10–80% time approximate.
Compact electric Subaru. Premium FWD is $34,995 / 308 mi. Not rated to tow.

Three-row electric SUV. There is no plug-in minivan on the US market anymore; this and the Kia EV9 are the closest family haulers. Peak DC 233 kW and 10.9 kW home charging per Hyundai spec and US reports.
Mercedes' new entry EV, effectively replacing the EQB. 374 mi is the best-case configuration.
Deliveries began spring 2026 with the launch edition. Cheaper trims follow: Premium ~$53,990 (late 2026), Standard ~$44,990–48,490 (2027). Home charging rate (~11.5 kW) is unconfirmed.
Standard AWD. MSRP approximate (sources vary $40,325–40,825).
Standard AWD. Whether MSRP includes destination is unconfirmed.
Three-row plug-in hybrid. Seat count, cargo, and towing unconfirmed.
The only 7-seat plug-in hybrid under ~$45k. Charges slowly at home (3.3 kW, ~6.5 hours on Level 2). DC fast charging uses CHAdeMO, which few US stations still support.
